summary_verdict: The combined performance optimization and exact rectangle error-map reuse are confirmed local runtime improvements with identical output. Rate-aware allocation at 500k/35, weight 0.4, is a credible measured RD research lead that survives this holdout under interpolated existing-frontier comparisons. It is not a release improvement: encoding remains slower than released HQ, regressions persist, and most holdout matches are not tight actual-rate pairs. Weight 0.8 does not generalize convincingly.
allocation_verdict: The weight-0.4 integrated selector improves the observed/estimated rate-distortion frontier on most tested images, beyond a better local proxy score: final files are serialized, decoded and measured on all 25 images. Relative to the strongest previous measured release/current envelope, mean interpolated matched-rate MSE changes -5.16% on main (17/20 wins) and -9.26% on holdout (4/5 wins). This merits continued research, with explicit latency and sparse-curve limits. No universal default or PBC 3.1 release is accepted.
allocation_interpretation: Main weight-0.4 output is 138.4631 MSE at 0.321073 bpp, 0.8055 s encode and 0.1125 s decode. Ordinary 500k/35 is 128.6912 MSE at 0.403293 bpp, 0.7605/0.1174 s: this is an operating-point quality/rate tradeoff with 5.92% additional encoding cost. Released HQ is 143.1334 MSE at 0.542457 bpp, 0.6410/0.1861 s, so the candidate has lower main mean MSE and rate but is 25.65% slower to encode. Holdout weight 0.4 has 59.0152 MSE at 0.697512 bpp, compared with ordinary 500k/35's 43.9331 at 1.019742: absolute quality is worse at much lower rate, despite the matched-rate estimated improvement. Working resolution, precision, patch counts and evolving geometry interact; excessive grids are part of the inefficiency, not free redundant information. The fixed/integrated comparison supports a real sequential effect at weight 0.4, while weight 0.8 demonstrates that local efficiency and stronger rate pressure can fail globally.
search_verdict: Rectangle reuse preserves all 100 default image/preset streams and decoded pixels on all three full repeats. Full encode latency, including per-call prototype state/installation/cleanup, changes -6.80% on main (72/80 case wins) and -5.99% on holdout (17/20). The average prototype installation is about 1.10 ms, included. This is a meaningful local runtime-only improvement; decoder differences are noise. It remains unvalidated on HF and requires explicit per-encode state ownership before concurrent production integration.
sequential_answer: The effect is not confined to static local scores. Integrated weight 0.4 improves mean matched-rate MSE versus the measured fixed-geometry family by 5.06% on 17 overlapping main images (14 wins) and 16.61% on all five holdout images. These are sparse interpolated comparisons, not a continuous dominance proof. Both integrated settings change geometry on all 25 images. Weight 0.8 loses versus that family on average, particularly on holdout, so the effect depends on the sequential policy rather than following automatically from the proxy.
frontier_answer: Against release default Q-HQ brackets, integrated weight 0.4 gives estimated MSE -11.26% on 15 main overlaps (13 wins), and -10.34% on two holdout overlaps (two wins). Against the broader strongest previously measured envelope, it gives -5.16% on all 20 main and -9.26% on all five holdout images. Seven main images have a previously measured point within 5% rate, with six MSE wins; holdout has only one such point, also a win. The observed frontier expands in a useful but content-dependent way; denser actual matched-rate controls are required to establish its size securely.
holdout_answer: The weight-0.4 interpolated all-rate signal survives: four of five holdout images improve, while pigeon.JPG regresses about 18.88% against the strongest existing envelope. Only two holdout cases fall specifically within release Q-HQ neighbor brackets, so broad high-quality generalization remains uncertain. Weight 0.8 is essentially neutral on that holdout envelope (-0.05% mean) and is not a convincing follow-up candidate.
outlier_answer: Large regressions are reduced in some cases but not eliminated. Weight 0.4 still has strongest-envelope matched-rate regressions of about +25.24% on mario64.png, +12.02% on monet.jpg, +10.25% on eiffel.png and +18.88% on holdout pigeon.JPG. Different rates/control envelopes make direct percentages versus Pass 2 outliers non-equivalent; do not claim those failures solved. Stronger weight 0.8 creates additional trajectory/entropy failures, including the 15k_kills raw/final-size reversal.
pbc31_answer: Smarter allocation within the existing v0 format is a credible PBC 3.1 research path: one small deterministic rule improves actual-file estimated RD on main and frozen holdout, without new models, proposals or decoder syntax. It has not met the release bar because of encoding cost, content regressions, sparse matching and untested HF behavior.
limitation_answer: The measured limitation is an interaction of representation cost, the one-action model's chosen geometry, ordinary early stopping and later residual states. Zero sampled cheap alternatives locally dominate the original, so simply declaring HQ precision wasted is unsupported. Fine detail still costs real SSE reduction; rate allocation can trade that reduction usefully on some trajectories. This pass does not isolate a fundamental representation-capacity ceiling or establish that a PBC 4.0 format is required.
next_rd_experiment: First add tightly bracketing ordinary-codec controls near the frozen weight-0.4 operating points, including the difficult synthetic/texture/pigeon cases and new independent images, to test interpolation sensitivity. If that signal persists, test one output-preserving reduction in selector cost: reuse the projected residual grid when evaluating a lower-precision palette. Keep the geometry count, model, seed, rate weight and stop rule fixed for that cost ablation; do not add a new beam or retraining.
strategic_answer: Prioritize PBC 3.1 runtime/allocation refinement and authorized HF validation. The existing-format lead makes a fundamental PBC 4.0 rewrite premature. Standalone decoder packaging is useful but a broad native rewrite is lower priority than validating the measured NumPy/grid and exact map improvements; PIL bicubic compatibility and the remaining native operations must be preserved in any port.
classification: Runtime-only strict output preservation: combined grid/MSE option and rectangle reuse. Estimated observed RD lead with a latency cost: weight-0.4 integrated allocation. Operating-point rate-for-quality tradeoffs: both allocation weights versus ordinary 500k/35. Negative/inconclusive generalization: weight 0.8, universal HQ250 selection, content routing and HF transfer. Fixed-geometry replay is an expensive diagnostic, not a shipping encoder. No strict all-metric production release is declared.
next_steps:
1. With separate authorization, run the supplied hash-checked private cpu-basic benchmark for grid/skip/both; validate rectangle reuse separately in a serial worker before any production state ownership change. Keep public UI MSE enabled.
2. Validate the frozen weight-0.4 RD lead with denser matched-rate ordinary controls and new images, then independently reduce its extra action-evaluation cost through projection reuse. Retain the named regression cases.
3. After those independent gates, test a controlled composition of the proven runtime changes with the allocation candidate. Measure the combination directly; do not add speed percentages or claim that runtime improvements repair RD regressions. A universal classifier, broader model or new stream representation is not the next justified step.
